text: A portent is a sign that something important, usually bad, is coming. Here Lake Chad's shrinking was read as an early warning of climate collapse, a warning that proved wrong.
Inexorable means impossible to stop, like a slow tide. Here it describes the old belief that the Sahel was drying out in a way nobody could halt.
To compound a problem is to make it worse by piling something on top of it. Here droughts shrank Lake Chad and farm irrigation drained it further.
Lake Chad is a large shallow lake on the edge of the Sahara, shared by Chad, Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria. It shrank dramatically and is now growing again.
The Sahel is the dry belt of land south of the Sahara, running from Senegal to Sudan. It is semi-arid: too wet to be desert, too dry for lush farmland.
The Sahara in north Africa is the world's largest hot desert. People long feared it was creeping south into the Sahel.
The Sudd is a vast wetland in South Sudan, Africa's biggest. It has swollen so much since 2020 that the landscape may be permanently changed.
Lake Turkana, in Kenya, is the world's largest permanent desert lake, meaning a lake that never dries up even though it sits in a desert.
A dramatic phrase for the climate changing so badly that societies and nature break down. Here it shows how scary Lake Chad's shrinking looked.
A number between 20 million and 99 million. It shows how many people relied on the lake for water, food and work.
Punishing means harsh and exhausting, causing great hardship. Punishing droughts are severe ones that hurt people and land badly.
A drought is a long period with much less rain than normal, leaving rivers, lakes and soil dry.
Diversion means sending something, here water, in a different direction. Farmers channelled the lake's water into fields, leaving less in the lake.
Irrigation is supplying water to crops through channels or pipes instead of waiting for rain.
Destined means seeming certain to end up a particular way, as if fate had decided. People thought the lake was destined to vanish.
To ravage is to damage something very badly, like a fire or storm. Famines ravaged the Sahel in the 1980s.
A famine is an extreme shortage of food that leaves many people starving across a region.
A preview is an early glimpse of what is coming. A grim one is a gloomy glimpse, here of a hotter, drier Africa that never fully arrived.
The part of a lake's surface that is clear water, not marsh, reeds or land. Scientists measure it from satellite pictures.
A general term for lakes, rivers, ponds and other collections of water.
A wetland is land soaked with water for much of the year, such as a marsh. Wetlands shelter wildlife and soak up floods.
Swollen means grown larger than usual, like a river after heavy rain. The Sudd marshes have expanded a lot.
For good means permanently. The idea is that the changed landscape may never go back to how it was.
To hint at something is to suggest it without saying it outright. Rising lakes hint at how Africa's climate may change.
Very hard to know. Scientists are saying they cannot say confidently how the climate will play out.
To adapt is to change how you live or work to suit new conditions. Climate adaptation means preparing for a changed climate, for example with flood defences.
COP31 is the 31st annual UN climate summit, where countries negotiate how to tackle climate change. COP stands for Conference of the Parties.
Clear-cut means obvious and certain, with no doubt. The article contrasts clear-cut changes like heat with uncertain ones like rain.
Glaciers are huge, slow-moving rivers of ice. Africa has only a few, on its highest mountains, and they are disappearing.
A heatwave is a spell of unusually hot weather lasting several days or more.
Periods of unusually hot weather, another word for heatwaves.
Here extreme has a technical meaning: a measure combining how long a hot spell lasts, how hot it gets, and how big an area it covers.
The WMO is the UN agency that coordinates weather and climate science around the world.
A smaller part of a larger region. Africa is often divided into sub-regions such as west, east and southern Africa.
Semi-arid land is quite dry, with some rain but not enough for lush forests or easy farming.
A rain gauge is a simple tool that measures how much rain falls. Calling the lake a giant one means its size shows how rainy the region is.
A monsoon is a seasonal wind that brings moist air from the ocean and heavy rain to land. The west African monsoon feeds the Sahel's rain.
To fuel something is to feed it and make it stronger. Warming seas and desert fuel the monsoon.
Moisture is water in the air or soil, in tiny amounts.
To revive is to come back to life or strength. Dry land reviving means plants growing again.
Groundwater is water stored underground in soil and rock, which people reach with wells.
Carrying off with great force. Floodwater sweeps away homes and villages.
Flash floods are sudden floods, often from very heavy rain, that give people little warning.
Niamey is the capital of Niger, a Sahel country, and sits beside the Niger River.
Desertification is the process of fertile land turning into desert. The article says the belief that it was relentless is now challenged.
Relentless means never easing or stopping.
The period when European powers ruled much of Africa, mostly the 1800s to the mid-1900s. Some ideas about Africa's environment began then.
A savannah is a warm grassland with scattered trees.
A premise is an idea you accept as true and build an argument or plan on. If the premise is wrong, the plan may be too.
An African Union project to plant trees and restore land across the Sahel to hold back the desert.
Soil losing its fertility or being blown or washed away, making it harder to grow crops.
The scientist means that climate change looks different in each place: wetter here, drier there, so plans must fit local conditions.
Data means measurements and records. Without enough reliable data, scientists cannot say what is really changing.
Dwindled means gradually got smaller or fewer. The long rains weakened over about 25 years.
East Africa's main rainy season, March to May, which farmers depend on to plant crops. The short rains come October to December.
Computer simulations of the atmosphere and oceans that scientists use to project how the climate may change.
A paradox is something that seems to contradict itself. Models predicted a wetter east Africa while the long rains actually dried up.
To dub something is to give it a nickname or name, as scientists did with this puzzle.
The Great Rift Valley is a long trench in east Africa where the earth's crust is slowly pulling apart. Many lakes fill it.
A projection is a forecast of what will likely happen based on current information and models, usually looking years ahead.
Here unsettled means not yet decided or agreed, with no clear answer. Scientists cannot yet say what will happen.
Magnitude means size or scale. Not knowing the magnitude means not knowing how big the change will be.
The mid-latitudes are the regions between the tropics and the poles, such as Europe and most of the US. Their weather is easier to model.
A dearth is a serious lack of something. Here there are too few weather observations in Africa.
Places with instruments that record rain, temperature and wind. Africa has few, and many do not work well.
To hasten something is to make it happen sooner or faster.
El Niño is a climate pattern in which the Pacific Ocean warms unusually, changing weather worldwide. In east Africa it often brings heavy rain and floods.
To engulf is to surround and cover completely. The lake's rising water has swallowed buildings.
Lake Baringo is a freshwater lake in Kenya's Rift Valley whose waters have been rising since 2010.
